clue.text: Confused tea with orangeade initially? Sign of nerves

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of orangeade is used

parts.note: first letter of orangeade
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone at a café, tea and orangeade in hand, gets flustered and twitchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in total disorder, the state of a muddled, bewildered mind or scene.

clue.text: Murderer grabs appropriate leader

indicators.note: grabs means the murderer holds the next word inside him

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A killer seizing a suitable chief, perhaps as a hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the head of a team or ship, its leader.

clue.text: Comes and goes far?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gets to a place
second meaning: achieves success, as one who has arrived in a career

explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes and goes' looks like a pair of opposites; it is two meanings of one word, the second being to make it big.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both reaching a destination and becoming established or successful.

clue.text: Something prickly ripped clothing horrendously at first

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the ripped word goes round the next letter

parts.note: torn means ripped

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of horrendously is wanted

parts.note: first letter of horrendously

explanation.surface: A spiky bush that has torn someone's clothes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' is not garments but the act of covering: TORN wraps round H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem such as a rose.

clue.text: Red tonic mum's drunk

indicators.note: drunk means jumbled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Mother has been drinking the tonic water.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour long linked with left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is an informal term for a socialist or Marxist, hence a member of that party.

clue.text: Since start of Brexit, Spain imports sauce, strangely

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of Brexit is wanted

parts.note: first letter of Brexit
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of sauce are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A news item: after Brexit, Spain has started importing some sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imports' works only as a link word here; Spain's letter is simply followed by the rearranged sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Since and because are both conjunctions giving a reason, so one swaps for the other.

clue.text: Move bird? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I says the letter I is taken out of the bird

parts.note: a budgie (budgerigar) is a small pet parrot

explanation.surface: Someone asked to shift the bird refuses: not me!
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move slightly, usually in the negative 'won't budge'.

clue.text: Make prisoners almost honest in front of court

indicators.note: in front of places the preceding pieces before the court

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the honest word is dropped

parts.note: true means honest or faithful

explanation.surface: Convicts who are nearly truthful are made to go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct is to build or make something.

clue.text: Mythical creature Greek character picked up — one with growth on foot?

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one
a corn is a hard growth on the foot

explanation.surface: A Greek person picked up by a beast with a lump on its hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse with a single horn, a creature of myth.

clue.text: Call hospital department that is nursing tense student

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so IE goes around the next letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A hospital ward where staff are caring for an anxious student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' fits the hospital scene but means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book is to name or call it.

clue.text: Work for each group of schoolchildren

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'two per person'
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A worksheet handed out to every class in the school.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or engine that works or functions well can be said to perform.

clue.text: One maybe treating canine with biscuit, finally — it ends barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of biscuit is used

parts.note: last letter of biscuit

explanation.surface: A dog given a biscuit to stop it barking, perhaps at the vet's.
explanation.walkthrough: The canine is a tooth, not a dog. The letters T, IT and ENDS are mixed to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is a pointed tooth, and the professional who looks after teeth is this one; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Approach banker, creating excitement

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming, an approach
a banker is a river (it has banks); the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Pitching an idea to a bank manager, with all the thrill that brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an exciting experience, so the word can stand for thrills or excitement.

clue.text: Time before river revealed fish

indicators.note: before puts the time letter ahead of what follows

parts.note: out means made known or revealed, as a secret is out

explanation.surface: An angler's tale: a fish finally showed itself in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Ink discharging both ends — a pen's dreadful

indicators.note: discharging both ends means the first and last letters of ink are dropped

parts.note: ink with both ends gone
a pen, as for pigs, is a sty; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A fountain pen leaking ink at both ends makes a horrible mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and dreadful are synonyms for something very unpleasant.

clue.text: Shaver's gone rusty, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A razor has corroded, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaver' looks like a razor; it is an old word for a lad, as in 'young shaver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaver is a dated informal term for a boy, a youth or child.

clue.text: Flung niece out with no good effect

indicators.note: out says the letters of flung niece are thrown into a new order
with no says one letter must be left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: Someone hurled their niece out, with no good outcome at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from FLUNG NIECE and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence is the power to have an effect on someone or something, so the two nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: In favour of Democrat interrupting US president getting banned

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the president's name

parts.note: Joe Biden was the 46th US president

explanation.surface: A political story: a Democrat butting into the president's business ends up barred.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidden means prohibited or not allowed, the same as banned.

clue.text: Meet in Parisian bar

parts.note: en is French for in
a counter is a bar, as in a shop or pub

explanation.surface: An invitation to rendezvous in a bar in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them, often by chance.

clue.text: Forgave former lover and swore to ignore king

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to ignore says one letter is skipped from the swearing word

parts.note: cursed means swore
R is the abbreviation for king (rex)

explanation.surface: An ex-partner who forgave and then cursed, though not at the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone's fault is to pardon or overlook it.

clue.text: Under church, climbers will find badgers

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the climbers beneath the church

parts.note: ivies are climbing plants

explanation.surface: Wildlife beneath a church, where mountaineers might spot badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badgers' is the verb, to nag; chivvies is the commoner spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To chivy someone is to pester or nag them, which is what badgering means.

clue.text: Some pretty pessimistic characters

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a group of rather gloomy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Types and characters both mean sorts of person, as in 'odd types' or 'odd characters'.

clue.text: Retiring soldier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shy, keeping to oneself
second meaning: a soldier of the lowest rank

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a soldier leaving the army; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both secluded or reserved and an ordinary rank-and-file soldier.

clue.text: Subdivision from group including FBI agents

indicators.note: including says the group holds the agents inside it

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are US federal agents

explanation.surface: A unit of a team that has FBI agents in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or section, one subdivision of a whole.

clue.text: Stick with cold swimmer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a ling is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Advice to stay with a chilly swimmer, perhaps one in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish; the ling is a long fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to stick fast or adhere tightly to something.

clue.text: Substituting western pine with grass outside

indicators.note: outside means the grass word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to sing
to itch for something is to long or pine for it

explanation.surface: A gardener swapping a western pine tree for a lawn around it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'pine' and 'grass' are verbs here, not plants: to long for, and to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching one thing for another is replacing or substituting it.

clue.text: Kind Liberal bandaging eye infection? On the contrary

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping around something
on the contrary reverses the wrapping: the infection goes round the Liberal, not the other way

parts.note: a stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid

explanation.surface: A kindly Liberal politician dressing someone's sore eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, L would wrap STYE; 'On the contrary' flips it so STYE holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Style can mean a kind or sort, as in a style of music.

clue.text: Twice actor oddly rejected a drink

indicators.note: twice says the letters from the actor are written down two times in a row
oddly rejected means the odd-placed letters of actor are thrown out, keeping the even ones

parts.note: even letters of actor

explanation.surface: A performer twice turned down for odd behaviour has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from cacao powder.

clue.text: Writer left with yen, quickly

parts.note: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An author who walked out with Japanese money in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftly and quickly are synonymous adverbs of speed.

clue.text: State dept half abandoned Irish county

indicators.note: half abandoned means only the first half of dept is kept

parts.note: first half of dept
Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A government department has half pulled out of a county in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun going with 'dept', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state or announce it formally.

clue.text: Justify Edward returning first tennis shot

indicators.note: first puts the turned name ahead of the tennis shot
returning says the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed is the short form of Edward
a serve is the stroke that starts a tennis point

explanation.surface: Edward coming back with a good first serve proves he merits his place.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, and justifying a reward is earning or deserving it.

clue.text: Stores are in retreat? Most close

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so the retreat word contains the other

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether shops are retreating, closing branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' looks like a noun meaning shops, but it is the verb meaning keeps or holds, and 'retreat' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, so it means closest or most close.
